issues: Numbers reproduce EXACTLY on re-run (driver + model self-test both clean). The control is genuinely meaningful, not vacuous: lam=0 exercises the full CVaR branch (eta/u vars instantiated) but weights it out, so max_diff=0 is the correct, non-trivial generalisation check. NO band-collapse, no secretly-equal baseline, no implausible monotonicity in the headline result. ONE real defect, in INTERPRETATION not data: the 'alpha insensitivity' finding is explained as an empirical artefact of a 'smooth scenario distribution'. That is wrong. It is a mathematical CERTAINTY of the design: with exactly 3 scenarios where the worst-cost atom has weight 0.3, and alpha in {0.7,0.8,0.9} => (1-alpha) in {0.3,0.2,0.1} all <= 0.3, CVaR_alpha collapses identically to the single worst-scenario cost for ALL three alphas. Verified directly (single planning step: identical objective 0.85422 across all alpha) and analytically (R-U LP on toy costs [1,2,5] w=[.3,.4,.3] gives CVaR=5.0=worst for every alpha tested). The alpha sweep is structurally INCAPABLE of differentiating - a vacuous sweep DIMENSION. To make alpha bite you need the tail mass (1-alpha) to slice INTO a finer atom than the 0.3 worst weight, i.e. more scenarios or unequal weights, not 'fatter tails'. The 'free lunch' (lam 0.25-0.75 lowers mean) is REAL and robust (reproduced with larger magnitude at seeds 7 and 123): it is the standard closed-loop MPC effect that the plan minimising expected forecast-scenario cost is not the plan minimising realised-truth cost, so a CVaR tilt can luck into better t=0 actions. lam=1.0 over-hedge is also robust across seeds.
final_takeaways: CONTROL VALID (not vacuous): lam=0 reproduces cvar=None to max_diff=0.0 while still instantiating the CVaR eta/u machinery - a real generalisation check. Re-run reproduced every cell of the table exactly; model.py self-test passes.

CORRECTION to the prior agent's headline: the alpha-insensitivity is NOT an empirical 'smooth distribution' finding - it is a structural artefact of using only 3 scenarios with a 0.3-weight worst atom. For alpha in {0.7,0.8,0.9}, (1-alpha) in {0.3,0.2,0.1} all <= 0.3, so CVaR_alpha is IDENTICALLY the worst-scenario cost for every alpha. The sweep cannot differentiate by construction. Proven at a single planning step (identical objective) and analytically.

Consequence: this experiment provides ZERO information about alpha tuning. Do not conclude 'alpha is immaterial in general'. To actually probe alpha you must add scenarios (e.g. 5-7 PV quantiles) or unequal weights so the tail mass 1-alpha cuts into a finer-than-0.3 atom; alpha=0.95 would still collapse to worst here. 'Pick 0.8' is an acceptable default but rests on no evidence from this run.
lam=1.0 (pure CVaR) over-hedges: mean +0.088 (+4.8%) AND p95 +0.028 - it raises BOTH, so it is strictly dominated. Robust across seeds 42/7/123 (deltas +0.07 to +0.08). Avoid lam=1.

Partial blend lam in {0.25,0.5,0.75} lowers mean ~0.014 and p95 ~0.0024 vs baseline. This is genuine and robust (seeds 7/123 show -0.029 to -0.049 on mean), and is the expected closed-loop MPC realised-vs-planned divergence, not a solver fluke. Treat it as 'mild CVaR blending is harmless-to-slightly-helpful here', not as a guaranteed free lunch in deployment.

Recommended Phase 2 setting from THIS evidence: a light blend lam ~= 0.25 (lightest blend achieving the mean/p95 improvement); alpha is unconstrained by this experiment so leave at a conventional 0.8 but flag that it was never actually exercised. Re-run with >=5 scenarios before making any alpha claim in EMHASS #841.
